# Tidy Code

First run our library list (Install first if you don't have these
packages).

```{r}
#Install and library important packages
#install.packages('ggplot2')
#install.packages('ggeffects')
#install.packages('RColorBrewer')
#install.packages('here')
#install.packages('MASS')
#install.packages('tidyverse')
#install.packages('janitor')
#install.packages('readxl')
#install.packages('brms')
library(ggeffects)
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(brms)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(tibble)
library(MASS)
```

### Importing the data sheet

```{r}
behavior_sheet <- read_excel("UW_Nest_Behavioral_Sheets_Cleaned.xlsx")
head(behavior_sheet)
```

### Separating the date column and placing it near the original Date column for filtering ease later on.

```{r}
behavior_sheet_date <- as.Date(behavior_sheet$Date)
behavior_sheet$Date <- behavior_sheet_date
behavior_sheet_sep <- behavior_sheet %>%
  mutate(Year = year(Date)) %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date)) %>%
  mutate(Day = day(Date)) %>%
  relocate(Year, .after = Date) %>%
  relocate(Month, .after = Year) %>%
  relocate(Day, .after = Month)
head(behavior_sheet_sep)

#Fix SAT submission to NM from chr to num
sat_sub <- as.numeric(behavior_sheet_sep$`SAT submission to NM`) #Creates a vector with the same entries but as numbers
behavior_sheet_sep$`SAT submission to NM` <- sat_sub #put it back into the tibble
#Do the same for SNK Submission to SAT
snk_sub <- as.numeric(behavior_sheet_sep$`SNK submission to SAT`)
behavior_sheet_sep$`SNK submission to SAT` <- snk_sub
#Same for NM aggression to SAT
NM_aggsat <- as.numeric(behavior_sheet_sep$`NM aggression to SAT`)
behavior_sheet_sep$`NM aggression to SAT` <- NM_aggsat
```

### Create a tibble with cleaned names

This chunk will be useful when creating and running models later on
because it "standardizes" the column names.

```{r}
behavior_sheet_cln <- behavior_sheet_sep |>
  #Uses the Janitor package to standardize the names
  clean_names()

#Turn the year variable into a character for ease of comparison later on
year_date <- as.character(behavior_sheet_cln$year) #Creates a vector with years as chr
behavior_sheet_cln$year <- year_date #creates a new variable for ease of graphing later on
```

### Social Environment sizes
We want to get an understanding about how the size of the social environment affects female mate choice. First, let's calculate the size of the social environment
```{r}
behave_sheet_social_size <- behavior_sheet_cln |>
  mutate('social_env_size' = 2 + average_snk + total_female_visits) #Gives us an estimates social environment size at the nest
```

Then we want to see if the number of females that spawned correlates with social environment size
```{r}
f_visits_envsize <- behave_sheet_social_size |>
  ggplot(aes(social_env_size, total_female_spawning)) + #gives ggplot dimensions
  geom_point() + #makes the plot a scatterplot
    geom_smooth(method = (lm)) +
  labs(title = 'Total Number of Females that Spawned as Function of Social Environment Size',
       x = 'Social Environment Size',
       y = "Total Females that Spawned") +
  theme_classic() + #Sets the plot visuals
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) #Moves title to the middle
  

f_visits_envsize
```

```{r}
fspawn.socenvsize.mdl <-
  brm(data = behave_sheet_social_size, #Give the model the tibble
      family = gaussian, #Tell model what type of distribution
      total_female_spawning ~ social_env_size, #Specifying the model
      iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, chains = 4, cores = 4, #Markov chain parameters
      seed = 4, #Determines which random numbers
      file = 'Exploratory model outputs/fspawn.socenvsize.mdl') #saves it as an output

summary(fspawn.socenvsize.mdl)
plot(fspawn.socenvsize.mdl)
```
Based on our results, we see that given our model, we can suggest that for every additional individual at a nest, there is a 0.36 increase in number of females that spawn at a nest. Our 95% credibility interval gives us 0.31-0.41, allowing us to suggest that this effect is different from zero. 

What about how many times a female spawns

```{r}
f_tspawns_envsize <- behave_sheet_social_size |>
  ggplot(aes(social_env_size, total_spawns)) + #gives ggplot dimensions
  geom_point() + #makes the plot a scatterplot
  geom_smooth(method = (lm)) +
  labs(title = 'Total Spawns as Function of Social Environment Size',
       x = 'Social Environment Size',
       y = "Total Spawns") +
  theme_classic() + #Sets the plot visuals
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) #Moves title to the middle
  

f_tspawns_envsize
```



```{r}
fmultispawn.socenvsize.mdl <-
  brm(data = behave_sheet_social_size, #Give the model the tibble
      family = gaussian, #Tell model what type of distribution
      total_spawns ~ social_env_size, #Specifying the model
      iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, chains = 4, cores = 4, #Markov chain parameters
      seed = 4, #Determines which random numbers
      file = 'Exploratory model outputs/fmultispawn.socenvsize.mdl') #saves it as an output

summary(fmultispawn.socenvsize.mdl)
plot(fmultispawn.socenvsize.mdl)
```
Based on our results, we see that given our model, we can suggest that for every additional individual at a nest, there is a 0.53 increase in number times a female will spawn at a nest. Our 95% credibility interval gives us 0.44-0.60, allowing us to suggest that this effect is different from zero.
